Q: SUM(amount) not working when also calling base column amount in SELECT clause A:

Since there are no window functions in MS Access, calculate the totals by item_id with an additional query.

SELECT *
FROM (
    SELECT location_id, item_id, amount
    FROM location_item
    WHERE location_id = 1
    GROUP BY item_id, location_id,amount
)t1
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT item_id, SUM(amount) AS total
    FROM location_item
    GROUP BY  item_id
)t2 ON t1.item_id=t2.item_id
location_id t1.item_id amount t2.item_id total
1 1 400 1 1000
1 2 300 2 300
1 3 200 3 200

If table "location_item" big enough, use indexes and subquery to limit rows in "total" subquery.

SELECT *
FROM (
    SELECT location_id, item_id, amount
    FROM location_item
    WHERE location_id = 1
    GROUP BY item_id, location_id,amount
)t1
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT item_id, SUM(amount) AS total
    FROM location_item
    WHERE item_id IN (SELECT item_id  FROM location_item  WHERE location_id = 1)
    GROUP BY  item_id
)t2  on t1.item_id=t2.item_id

Q: How to organise all the data from SEC.Gov Edgar API into instatement and balance sheet A:

The grouping isn't something you have to invent. The filer already declared it, in the filing's presentation linkbase, and the SEC publishes that flattened.

Easiest route is the Financial Statement Data Sets (the quarterly zips). Two files matter. num.txt holds every value (adsh, tag, ddate, value). pre.txt says where each tag was presented, and that's the bit you want: it has a stmt column (BS, IS, CF) and a line number for the order.

Join them on adsh and tag:

import pandas as pd

num = pd.read_csv("num.txt", sep="\t", low_memory=False)

pre = pd.read_csv("pre.txt", sep="\t", low_memory=False)

df = num.merge(pre[["adsh","tag","stmt","line","plabel"]], on=["adsh","tag"])

inc = df[(df.adsh == ACCESSION) & (df.stmt == "IS")].sort_values("line")

That gives you each number sitting on the right statement, in the filer's own order. No hand-built concept map.

If you'd rather stay per filing, the same information lives in that filing's FilingSummary.xml, which lists the R-files (each one a rendered statement), and in the _pre.xml linkbase.

One thing worth knowing, since it explains your flat bag: companyfacts drops the presentation layer entirely. It's the easiest endpoint to pull, which is why everyone starts there, but it never says which statement a tag belongs on. That only exists in the linkbase or pre.txt.

(I run an API that does this grouping, but pre.txt is the real answer if you're building it yourself.)

It seems to me that what happened to Stack Overflow is that they added this Advice tag thingy?, and either 'moderation' or even bot puts it on 'every' question disallowing for answers, I think the era of asking questions here is over, this was my first and last one.

When you opened this question you apparently chose a Type of "General advice / Other" instead of the default "How to / Troubleshooting". The "How to / Troubleshooting" type is the traditional Stack Overflow question-and-answer post; all the other ones are a new type of "discussion" question where there are no separate answers and comments, just "replies". And, unfortunately, there's no way to edit the question to change the type: Can an Advice post be changed into a QA post (or vice versa)?

Currently you'd have to delete the question and then re-post it as a new "How to / Troubleshooting" question... which might trip up the automatic duplicate detection unless you wait some amount of time or change the wording and... anyway it's not a wonderful situation.

Q: Jenkins to List count of build for jenkins job A:

You can try global-build-stats plugin provided by Jenkins. It provides graphical representation for the total number of builds executed in each pipeline with more details like execution time, status, executor and more. You can also filter by adding start and end date.

https://plugins.jenkins.io/global-build-stats/
